md_docs_2mcp(3) Library Functions Manual md_docs_2mcp(3)

NAME

md_docs_2mcp - MCP rendering server

ascii-chat mcp-server exposes four rendering tools over newline-delimited JSON-RPC on stdio. It runs through the ordinary application initialization, options, logging, error-stack and diagnostic workers. Both transports automatically skip startup update checks. Protocol stdout is reserved before initialization; incidental terminal diagnostics go to stderr.

ascii-chat mcp-server --transport http serves all five tools at /mcp using MCP Streamable HTTP and libwebsockets. The default listener is 127.0.0.1:27228, following the native TCP and WebSocket defaults (27224–27227). Override it with --port, ASCII_CHAT_PORT, --address, --address6, or the existing zero-to-two positional IPv4/IPv6 bind addresses. Examples: 

ascii-chat mcp-server --transport http --port 28028 --address 127.0.0.1
ascii-chat mcp-server --transport http 0.0.0.0 ::1 --port 27228
ascii-chat --log-level debug --grep 'MCP|render' mcp-server --transport http --status-screen

The --http-tls-cert, --http-tls-key, and --http-tls-key-password configure HTTPS for this HTTP listener too. --port-forwarding maps the HTTP port with the existing UPnP implementation. Concurrent render jobs default to the number of CPUs available to the process; --max-clients can set a lower limit. HTTP status uses the shared terminal controller and log viewer, including error popups and debug controls. Debug builds retain --sync-state, --backtrace, and memory diagnostics. Stdio does not consume terminal keys: stdin is the protocol stream.

For mcp.ascii-chat.com, terminate HTTPS and enforce rate/body/concurrency limits at a reverse proxy. The configured browser Origin defaults to https://mcp.ascii-chat.com; change it with --http-origin. Requests without Origin are accepted for native MCP clients. The initial implementation uses stateless JSON responses; POST handles requests and notifications, GET/DELETE return 405. It supports MCP versions 2025-03-26, 2025-06-18, and 2025-11-25. Clients send Accept including application/json and text/event-stream.

Tools

  • render_file: exactly one of path or data_base64, optional mime_type. A source may be omitted when options select synthetic test video/audio.
  • render_url: url for media supported by the CLI FFmpeg/yt-dlp resolver.
  • device_list: no arguments. Returns video_devices and audio_devices (microphones), each with index, name, and is_default, plus default_video_device and default_audio_device (null when absent). Webcam default is index 0; microphone default comes from the OS. Enumeration failures appear in errors, preserving devices discovered in the other category. Hidden with --server.
  • render_webcam: optional video_device (default 0), audio_device (-1 or omitted uses the system microphone), and volume (microphone gain, 0 to 1). Timed saved exports capture microphone audio unless options.audio is false. options.test-pattern uses synthetic video instead.
  • render_visualization: visualization is waveform or fft; optional Audio selects { "type": "test" } (default), { "type": "file", "path": "..." }, { "type": "file", "data_base64": "...", "mime_type": "audio/wav" }, { "type": "url", "url": "..." }, or local { "type": "microphone" } with top-level audio_device: 0 and optional volume (0-1). Supplying audio_device or volume without an audio source selects microphone input. Both fields are unavailable with --server.

Rendering tools accept Options Module, timeout_ms (1000–60000, default 45000), and a local-only optional output_path. 

{


  "name": "render_file",


  "arguments": {


    "path": "/home/me/image.png",


    "options": {


      "width": 100,


      "height": 40,


      "color-mode": "none",


      "snapshot": true,


      "snapshot-delay": 0


    }


  }
}

For uploaded media, the client must read and base64-encode the bytes; an attachment in a conversation is not automatically accessible to an MCP server. This uses normal JSON tool arguments with no upload endpoint or public URL requirement. Decoded uploads are limited to 16 MiB; request bodies to 24 MiB; returned ASCII to 8 MiB.

The shared option schema is generated from the CLI registry through an explicit exposure table in src/mcp-server/request.c and the shared lib/options/json.c adapter. It covers palette/characters, color/filter/render mode, dimensions, transforms, effects, FPS, snapshot/delay, seek/loop, test pattern/audio, audio processing, and render styling. Local mode additionally exposes custom render fonts and yt-dlp options. Unsupported/unknown arguments are rejected, including arguments hidden from the hosted schema.

Defaults are 100×40, monochrome, snapshot enabled with delay zero, splash and speaker playback disabled. snapshot-delay measures capture duration after the first rendered frame, matching CLI semantics; it is not time from receipt of the tool call. Use seek to choose a media timestamp. Snapshot false is bounded by timeout and suitable for finite media; unbounded capture must finish via snapshot or returns a timeout error.

Saved images and videos

Video output automatically chooses a font size to keep large recordings near 1280 pixels per side. Set options.render-font-size (for example, 28) to choose an explicit size; width and height set the character grid. Images retain the 12-point default. Use color-mode for rendered colors, rather than the CLI diagnostic color option.

Set local output_path to an image/video filename. The existing render-file pipeline renders the ASCII grid into the encoded artifact, with format selected by extension. Parent directories must exist. The server stages the encoded artifact in a private directory beside the destination, then publishes with an atomic non-replacing hard link. Existing regular files, symlinks, and destinations won by concurrent writers are preserved. Filesystems without hard-link support return an error instead of falling back to an overwriting rename. Cancellation/failure removes staged artifacts; successful results contain absolute paths in structuredContent.saved_files. 

{


  "name": "render_visualization",


  "arguments": {


    "visualization": "fft",


    "audio": { "type": "test" },


    "options": { "snapshot": true, "snapshot-delay": 2, "render-font-size": 28, "color-mode": "truecolor" },


    "output_path": "/home/me/fft.mp4"


  }
}

Results contain content text plus structuredContent with ascii, elapsed_ms, and saved_files. Decoder/render errors use isError: true; JSON-RPC errors cover malformed protocol requests. Each render is isolated in a child mirror process with an explicit environment and no user/system configuration. The parent handles deadlines, output limits, and local cancellation while keeping its transport responsive.

Hosted isolation

--server mode omits device enumeration and webcam tooling and rejects caller-selected paths, microphone access, saved output paths, custom font paths, and arbitrary yt-dlp options. Uploaded bytes use private server-created temporary files. These capability restrictions do not sandbox third-party media decoders or URL extractors: public deployments must run under an unprivileged account/container with no secrets or device mounts and network egress rules blocking private/loopback/link-local/metadata destinations. Enforce those rules on redirected and nested media requests too. Put authentication/rate limits at the reverse proxy if required. Local mode intentionally permits the filesystem and devices of the user running it.

Codex connection

The repository's .codex/config.toml and .mcp.json use the shared HTTP endpoint http://127.0.0.1:27228/mcp. Start the runtime copy with build/bin/ascii-chat-mcp mcp-server --transport http --address 127.0.0.1 --port 27228 (Windows: add .exe). See the ascii-chat-mcp-dev skill for copying builds and restarting it. Chats retain the endpoint across restarts; interrupted requests may need retry.

For a client-managed stdio server instead:

[mcp_servers.ascii_chat]
command = "./build/bin/ascii-chat"
args = ["mcp-server", "--transport", "stdio"]
tool_timeout_sec = 70

The suffixless executable path works on Windows (which resolves .exe) and Unix (which uses the exact filename), without a symlink. For a checkout outside the current project, use its absolute suffixless path. Newly created chats can discover the five tools through this stdio connection. The server must be built before starting the chat.

Claude Code connection

To replace the shared HTTP entry in .mcp.json with a client-managed stdio server: 

{


  "mcpServers": {


    "ascii_chat": {


      "type": "stdio",


      "command": "./build/bin/ascii-chat",


      "args": [


        "mcp-server", "--transport", "stdio"


      ]


    }


  }
}

Build the executable first, start Claude Code from the checkout, and approve the project server when prompted. Use /mcp to inspect its connection. This is the same suffixless build path as the Codex configuration; use an absolute path for a server in another checkout.

For a networked server, start ascii-chat mcp-server --transport http --address 127.0.0.1 --port 27228 separately and replace the stdio entry with: 

{


  "mcpServers": {


    "ascii_chat": {


      "type": "http",


      "url": "http://127.0.0.1:27228/mcp"


    }


  }
}

Add --server for the restricted cloud tool profile described above. See the Claude Code MCP documentation for project scope and approvals.

Telemetry

MCP uses the ordinary --otel-* options, environment variables, configuration, and process shutdown. ascii-chat.mcp.request spans record bounded method and transport names; ascii-chat.mcp.render child spans preserve parent context across render threads and record the tool, output byte count, and failure category. HTTP responses record status codes and body sizes. Metrics under ascii-chat.mcp.* count requests, rejections, renders, failures, cancellations, deadlines, saved files, and output bytes, with render duration in seconds.

Telemetry attributes do not include media URLs, file paths, uploaded bytes, ASCII content, credentials, or caller-supplied request IDs. Render subprocesses keep their isolated environment and do not export separately; the parent records their job. As with every other mode, test environments prohibit collector export.

Statistics

MCP measurements use the process stats scope and canonical metric mappings in include/ascii-chat/stats/telemetry.def, so each observation feeds both local statistics and OTEL without duplicate counters. HTTP mode supports the = stats viewer, including totals, rates, render duration, and transport details. Use --stats-interval 1 with either transport for periodic summaries. MCP summaries use stderr so stdio stdout stays a JSON-RPC stream; stdio never reads UI keys.
